description: §4.14's own invalid example verbatim — an engine state-child `:`-shorthand body holding two semicolon-separated expressions (`<Idle : startGame(); track("start")>`) fires E-MULTI-STATEMENT-HANDLER. This pins the SECOND fire site (the `:`-shorthand body validator), distinct from the event-handler-attribute site pinned by `multi-stmt-handler-attr-pos`.
rationale: §4.14 ("What is NOT legal under `:`-shorthand"): "Multi-statement: `<Idle : startGame(); track()>` — `E-MULTI-STATEMENT-HANDLER`. Use bare-body." The S435 reversal of L19 (§5.2.3) legalised the inline BLOCK for event-handler attribute values only; §4.14 states it "does NOT reach `:`-shorthand bodies, which keep this single-expression rule". The §34 row (narrowed S435) keeps this locus as its shape (2): "a `:`-shorthand body (§4.14) containing multiple statements". The post-`:` body here carries a top-level `;`, so the code SHALL fire.
